correctness.rationale: Exact base-two digit pairing forces divisibility by three. The LTE identity gives nu_3(w_{m,j})=nu_3(2m-1-2j). The modulo-nine binomial expansion, residue counts of free coefficients and discrete Fourier inversion prove the exact three-component histogram for every m. Two free digit coefficients at valuation ell (distances 3^ell,5*3^ell) span all ternary changes modulo 3^(ell+1) without altering earlier digits. An explicit induction yields full residue coverage for all k>=2 and all m>=M_k. All low-index boundaries are included. Standalone exact verification tests 131071 palindromes, 2850 coefficient identities, and all 1092 explicit witnesses at k=2..7. Finite tests corroborate but are not the proof.

originality.rationale: No exact modulo-nine first-lift histogram or uniform exact-even-length 3-adic full-image theorem was identified in the reviewed prior literature or mathematical research records. Harminc-Sotak arithmetic-progression existence does not determine an exact-even-length full image or frequency. Tuxanidy-Panario assumes coprimality that excludes this case. Onphaeng et al. treat a base-congruence setting not applicable to base 2 modulo powers of 3. The closest publicly available exact result covers q|b+1, which for base two gives q=3 but cannot cover q=9,27,...; the known even-palindrome divisibility is credited. An unstated general implication is a residual risk.
residual_risks: The general arithmetic-progression construction might implicitly admit parity-preserving quantitative refinements not stated in the inspected text.
An unindexed or unpublished digit-automata result might already imply the exact modulo-nine distribution or the uniform all-level image.
No exhaustive search of every historical sequence or number theory table is possible; priority is assessed within inspected evidence.

value.rationale: A factor of three is forced by even-digit binary symmetry, motivating the natural question whether further 3-adic exclusions persist. The proven answer is a constructive all-level no-further-obstruction result holding at each sufficiently large exact even length, paired with a sharp, length-dependent first-lift frequency bias. The precise invariant and all-index bound are mathematically natural; the argument is not a routine finite table and the higher-level existence is genuinely infinite. The bound is explicitly not claimed optimal above the first lift.
